title: Fastest Animals in the World
intro: Speed depends on the medium. The fastest animals of all are birds in a hunting dive, where gravity does much of the work; in level flight, on land and in water the records are lower and belong to different animals. This ranking uses the best well-supported top speed for each animal in our database and tells you how that speed is reached, because a 300 km/h stoop and an 80 km/h sprint are not the same kind of fast.
method: Ranked by maximum recorded speed in km/h. Many popular figures are estimates from a single observation; where modern measurements disagree with an older claim we use the conservative value.

title: Fastest Land Animals
intro: On land the cheetah is the undisputed sprint champion, but it can hold top speed for only a few hundred meters. Several hoofed animals are nearly as fast and can keep going far longer, which is why pronghorn and antelope regularly outrun the predators that chase them. This ranking covers running speed only.
method: Animals whose top speed is achieved by running. Figures are short-burst maximums, not cruising speeds.

title: Fastest Birds
intro: Birds hold the outright animal speed records. The key distinction is between a stoop, a steep hunting dive with the wings folded, and powered level flight, which is much slower. Flightless birds are ranked by running speed.
method: Birds in our database ranked by maximum speed; the note beside each figure says whether it is a dive, level flight or running.

title: Fastest Sea Animals and Fish
intro: Water is about 800 times denser than air, so swimming speeds are far lower than flying or running speeds. They are also very hard to measure: the famous claims of sailfish and swordfish exceeding 100 km/h come from old fishing-line estimates, and modern tagging studies suggest much lower bursts. The figures here are the conservative, better-supported ones.
method: Animals whose top speed is achieved by swimming, ranked by maximum well-supported burst speed.

title: Longest-Living Animals
intro: The longest-lived animals share a few traits: they tend to be large, slow-growing, live in cold or stable environments, and have few predators as adults. Cold, deep water produces the most extreme cases, including a clam and a shark that live for centuries. This ranking uses the upper end of each animal's typical lifespan, in the wild or in human care, whichever is longer; one-off record individuals are mentioned on each animal's page.
method: Ranked by the upper end of the typical lifespan range (wild or captive, whichever is greater), converted to years.

title: Shortest-Living Animals
intro: At the other end of the scale are animals whose whole adult lives are measured in weeks. Most are insects and other small invertebrates, but some small mammals and fish also live fast: high metabolic rates, early breeding and heavy predation all go with a short life.
method: Ranked by the upper end of the typical wild lifespan, shortest first. For insects this is the adult stage or full life cycle as stated on each page.

title: Longest-Living Mammals
intro: Among mammals, lifespan rises with body size, but there are striking exceptions. Bowhead whales can live for two centuries, while the mouse-sized naked mole-rat outlives animals a thousand times heavier. Bats and primates also live much longer than their size predicts.
method: Mammals ranked by the upper end of the typical lifespan range, wild or captive, whichever is greater.

title: Heaviest Animals in the World
intro: The heaviest animals all live in the sea, where water supports their weight. The blue whale is the heaviest animal known to have existed, outweighing the largest land animal, the African elephant, by more than twenty times. On land the limits are set by legs and bones: no living land animal comes close to the great whales.
method: Ranked by the upper end of the typical adult weight range, converted to kilograms. Exceptional record individuals are not used.

title: Heaviest and Largest Birds
intro: The heaviest birds gave up flight altogether. Ostriches and emus are far heavier than any flying bird, because flight puts a hard ceiling on body weight: the heaviest fliers, such as swans, condors and albatrosses, top out at roughly 10 to 15 kilograms.
method: Birds ranked by the upper end of the typical adult weight range.

title: Smallest and Lightest Animals
intro: The lightest animals in our database weigh a fraction of a gram. Nearly all are insects, whose external skeletons and passive breathing systems work best at very small sizes. The smallest vertebrates here are hummingbirds, small frogs and aquarium fish.
method: Ranked by the upper end of the typical adult weight range, lightest first.

title: Tallest Animals in the World
intro: The giraffe is the tallest living animal by a wide margin, with adult males reaching well over five meters to the top of the head. This ranking mixes two kinds of measurement, and each row says which one applies: total standing height for animals such as giraffes, ostriches and penguins, and shoulder height for four-legged mammals such as elephants, moose and horses.
method: Animals measured by standing height or shoulder height, ranked by the upper end of the typical adult range in meters. Animals measured by body length are in the longest animals list instead.

title: Longest Animals in the World
intro: Length is the natural measure for whales, sharks, snakes, crocodiles and fish. The blue whale is the longest as well as the heaviest animal, and the longest snakes and the largest crocodiles are still small beside the great whales and the whale shark.
method: Animals measured by total or body length, ranked by the upper end of the typical adult range in meters. Widely repeated but unverified record lengths are not used.

title: Animals With the Longest Gestation Period
intro: Elephants have the longest pregnancy of any mammal, close to two years. Long gestation goes with large body size and with giving birth to a single, well-developed calf that can stand and follow the herd within hours. A few live-bearing sharks are thought to carry their young even longer, although their pregnancies are much harder to observe.
method: Live-bearing animals ranked by the upper end of the typical gestation period in days. Egg incubation times are not included.

title: Animals With the Shortest Gestation Period
intro: Short pregnancies belong to two groups. Marsupials such as kangaroos and koalas give birth after only a few weeks to tiny, undeveloped young that finish growing in the pouch. Small rodents and rabbits have short pregnancies and large litters, which lets them breed several times a year.
method: Live-bearing animals ranked by the upper end of the typical gestation period in days, shortest first.

title: Most Endangered Animals
intro: The IUCN Red List is the global standard for extinction risk. Species assessed as Critically Endangered face an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild, Endangered a very high risk, and Vulnerable a high risk. This list shows every animal in our database in those three threatened categories, most at risk first, with its population trend.
method: Animals assessed as Critically Endangered, Endangered or Vulnerable, ordered by category and then by population trend. Red List assessments are updated periodically; check the IUCN link on each animal page for the current assessment.
